title: Marble Madness
description: Atari's isometric marble-racing arcade classic in its Amiga port, decoded from the disk image with no emulation anywhere. The six courses come straight from their .mlb tilemaps with the engine's colour bands baked into recoloured atlas tiles and the gold shimmer replayed as tile animation; the scenery pieces (drawbridge, flags, the WAVE) are the Track files' own overlay scripts. Each course's true 3-D height field is rebuilt as a solid slope model with the Track-layer markers pinned on in colour — enemy routes, ooze spawns and scenery anchors. The themes are rendered by a from-scratch Go port of the game's music player.

assets.name: Practice slope
assets.description: The course's real 3-D terrain: the height field the physics rolls the marble on — every ramp, wall and pit — while the on-screen tilemap is only a picture of it. The coloured markers pin the course's other data layers onto the surface: cyan pins are scenery anchors, orange pins are ooze spawn points, yellow pins are scripted regions (drawbridges, funnels, triggers), and the magenta and green lines are the black marble's and the slinkies' patrol routes, each starting at its spawn pin.

assets.name: Out of time
assets.description: The tune the game-over sequence plays when the clock runs out. Every course's sound bank carries an identical copy as record 25, so the tune is on hand whichever bank is loaded; it is shipped here once.

assets.name: Score tally (Aerial bank)
assets.description: Played over the between-courses score tally, the time-bonus count-up. The tally trigger asks the loaded bank for this tune number; only this course's bank carries the record, so the other courses tally in silence.
